title: Air India Express Pilots Challenge Revised Pay Structure Over Income Uncertainty and Leave Cuts
excerpt: Despite higher headline earnings and fleet allowances, Air India Express pilots say the new compensation framework shifts rostering risk onto crews and effectively penalizes them for taking leave.
body:
• Air India Express pilots are pushing back against a revised compensation package that guarantees pay for only 40 hours of flying time, down from a pre-pandemic standard of 70 hours.
  • The Tata Group-owned carrier has offered Boeing 737 fleet allowances of up to Rs 21 lakh for senior commanders and raised earnings across ranks, but pilots say the structure ties income too heavily to monthly utilization.
  • A new leave framework effective April 2027 would cut Privilege Leave by six days, and pilots warn that taking approved leave could reduce variable pay — effectively penalizing them financially for time off.
  • The acceptance deadline for the revised terms was set for August 28, putting pressure on pilot groups to respond before the airline's planned fleet expansion.

Higher Pay, But Strings Attached

Air India Express has rolled out a revised compensation package that boosts headline earnings across pilot ranks and introduces new fleet-specific allowances, according to industry sources. Senior Commanders and Commanders on the Boeing 737 fleet stand to receive allowances of up to Rs 21 lakh, while Senior First Officers would get Rs 10 lakh — paid in three equal instalments over three years starting October 2026.

The package also includes revised productivity-linked pay rates, a narrow-body allowance of Rs 25,000 for P1 category pilots and Rs 10,000 for P2 pilots as part of fixed pay, and changes to base posting rules.

On paper, the numbers look better. But pilot representatives say the real concern lies in how those earnings are calculated.

The 40-Hour Guarantee Problem

Under the revised structure, Air India Express guarantees payment for only 40 hours of block flying time per month. Everything above that depends on actual monthly utilization — how much the airline chooses to schedule each pilot.

https://x.com/fl360aero/status/2093316527030186112

"Industry standards dictate that a pilot should be paid for the month, i.e. approximately 70 hours. A 40-hour commitment is highly unfair to the pilot."

— An Air India commander, speaking to Hindustan Times

Pilot representatives argue this arrangement shifts rostering and fleet deployment risk — factors entirely controlled by the airline — onto flight crew. Before the pandemic, the compensation model was built around 70 fixed flying hours, providing far greater income predictability. Pilots contend that a temporary reduction introduced during the Covid-19 period should not become the permanent structure.

A senior commander flying roughly 55 hours per month would earn about Rs 8.3 lakh under the revised framework, up from Rs 7.5 lakh previously, according to Aviation A2Z. A first officer on similar hours would take home around Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just above Rs 3 lakh. The increases are real — but so is the gap between guaranteed and potential pay.

Leave That Costs You Money

The airline has proposed a new leave structure effective April 1, 2027, comprising 24 Privilege Leave days, 12 Sick Leave days, and six Casual Leave days. That represents a reduction of six Privilege Leave days compared with the earlier structure.

Pilots have flagged what they see as a more fundamental problem: under the proposed pay model, taking Privilege Leave could reduce variable pay because of fewer flying hours in that month. Approved paid leave, in other words, could function as a salary cut.

Additional concerns include the treatment of night operations and Window of Circadian Low (WOCL) duties, compensation for positioning assignments and waiting time, and handling of lounge stays, tail swaps, and operations at critical airfields. Pilots say these responsibilities extend well beyond payable flying hours and should be reflected in the compensation framework.

Deadline Pressure as Fleet Grows

Revised offer letters were reportedly issued by August 14, with pilots required to communicate acceptance of the new terms by August 28, according to People Matters. The tight timeline adds pressure as Air India Express continues its fleet expansion and growth plans under the Tata Group's broader aviation strategy.

Earlier in August, the parent carrier Air India increased pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders receiving the largest raises. Under the group's restructuring, Air India Express is positioned as the main pathway for command upgrades on single-aisle fleets, while Air India offers progression into wide-body operations.

What to Watch

How Air India Express and its pilot groups resolve these concerns could shape workforce sentiment across the Tata aviation group. The dispute underscores a broader tension in Indian commercial aviation: airlines want productivity-linked pay to manage costs during fleet expansion, while pilots argue that income certainty is non-negotiable in a profession where scheduling and deployment are entirely employer-controlled.
